title: Food Safety & GMP Training
description: Onsite and virtual programs that embed Good Manufacturing and Hygienic Practices into daily operations and strengthen food-safety culture.

slides.detail: Tailored training programs for production staff, QA teams, and leadership that translate regulatory requirements into practical, day-to-day habits — building a facility-wide food safety culture rather than checkbox compliance.

Structured documentation of attendance, competency assessments, and certificates ensures your records hold up under CFIA, BRCGS, or customer audits — turning training into traceable evidence of due diligence.
Post-training evaluations identify knowledge gaps before they become operational risks. Scheduled refresher sessions keep food safety knowledge current as regulations evolve and staff roles change.

Generic training rarely sticks. Every program is anchored in your facility's actual workflows, product lines, and risk profile — making content immediately applicable and memorable for each team member.

title: Technical Training
tagline: Building technical confidence from farm to fork
description: Specialized trainings that strengthen analytical, processing, and quality skills across the full food production chain.

slides.detail: Understanding pathogen behavior, contamination routes, and microbiological testing methods is the foundation of a robust food safety program — this module bridges science and operational decision-making.
From thermal processing to modified atmosphere packaging, teams learn the critical control parameters that maintain product quality and safety — reducing spoilage, recalls, and consumer risk.

Canadian and international food legislation is complex and evolving. This module ensures your team understands the Safe Food for Canadians Regulations (SFCR), CFIA requirements, and how to stay current.
Learn how quality management systems — ISO 9001, BRCGS, SQF — integrate with regulatory requirements to create a cohesive framework that satisfies auditors and protects brand reputation.

With 14 priority allergens regulated in Canada, allergen management training covers risk assessment, cross-contact prevention, label verification, and crisis-response protocols that protect both consumers and your brand.
Equip your quality team to conduct thorough internal audits and use structured RCA methodologies (5-Whys, fishbone, FMEA) to resolve non-conformances before they escalate to regulatory action.

title: Quality System Documentation
description: Documentation that fits your operations — not a generic template dropped in your folder.

slides.detail: Standard Operating Procedures and Sanitation SOPs are developed in alignment with CFIA, Health Canada, and applicable global standards (BRCGS, SQF, FSSC 22000) — written in clear, actionable language your staff will actually use.

Procedures are mapped to your actual process flow — from receiving through dispatch — ensuring every step has an owner, a control, and a verification method that makes sense on the floor, not just on paper.
Records are formatted for easy retrieval, logical filing, and instant auditor-readiness — reducing the time your team spends scrambling during inspections and demonstrating a mature quality culture.

title: Laboratory Methods Advisory & Training
description: Building reliable, compliant laboratory systems through practical, results-focused programs.

slides.detail: Selecting validated, fit-for-purpose analytical methods — ISO, AOAC, or in-house — is critical for defensible results. Advisory covers method validation principles, detection limits, and regulatory acceptability.
Statistically sound sampling plans and rigorous data interpretation training ensure your laboratory results are reliable, reproducible, and meaningful for product release and compliance decisions.

Coordinating with accredited external labs — selecting the right lab, interpreting certificates of analysis, and managing turnaround times — reduces delays and ensures test results support your quality decisions.

When results are inconsistent or methods underperform, systematic troubleshooting identifies root causes — whether equipment drift, reagent quality, or procedural gaps — and implements optimized protocols.

title: Research Support
description: Structured guidance that enhances scientific rigor and publication credibility.

slides.detail: Robust research begins with a well-structured design. Support covers hypothesis formulation, experimental design (randomized, factorial, longitudinal), variable control, and protocol documentation to meet institutional and funder standards.

From descriptive statistics to multivariate analysis, guidance ensures the right tests are selected for your data type, assumptions are verified, and results are interpreted with appropriate confidence — strengthening peer-review outcomes.

Food and agri-food research often requires novel or adapted analytical methods. Support includes method development, preliminary validation, and documenting procedures to the level required for publication or regulatory submission.

Navigating journal-specific formatting guidelines, author contribution statements, and submission portals can derail otherwise excellent research. End-to-end submission support accelerates acceptance timelines.

Independent technical and language review catches errors, strengthens argument flow, and verifies originality — giving authors confidence their work will withstand peer scrutiny and editorial screening.

title: Proposal & Grant Development
description: Transforming research and industry concepts into funder-ready proposals.

slides.detail: Funders receive hundreds of submissions — clarity, logical flow, and technical accuracy are what make proposals stand out. Review services strengthen alignment between objectives, methodology, budget, and impact statements.

From NSERC and CIHR to provincial and industry-specific funds, grant-writing support covers narrative development, budget justification, and compliance with funder-specific eligibility and formatting requirements.
Rejected proposals contain valuable reviewer feedback that, when properly addressed, significantly improves resubmission success rates. Advisory translates reviewer critiques into targeted revisions.

title: Conference & Insight Support
description: Evidence-rich storytelling and impactful knowledge sharing for conferences and industry events.

slides.detail: From initial program design to on-the-day logistics, comprehensive conference support covers session structuring, speaker coordination, abstract management, and timeline planning that keeps events running flawlessly.

Data-driven visualizations, clean poster layouts, and compelling slide narratives ensure your research and industry insights reach audiences with clarity and impact — whether at academic conferences or industry summits.

Interactive workshop design and skilled facilitation create participatory learning environments that move beyond passive attendance — improving knowledge retention and generating actionable outcomes for diverse audiences.
Post-event impact documentation captures attendance, key learnings, and capacity outcomes — providing funders, stakeholders, and leadership with evidence of program value and return on investment.

title: Food Import Readiness & Compliance
description: Ensuring imported food products meet Canadian safety and labeling standards before they reach market.

slides.detail: Each food category — meat, dairy, produce, novel foods — has unique CFIA and Health Canada requirements. Advisory covers category-specific standards, permissible ingredients, and documentation requirements before product ships.

Import permits, certificates of free sale, phytosanitary certificates, and commercial invoices must align precisely with CFIA requirements at the border — this service prepares importers to avoid costly holds and rejections.

Recommending the right analytical tests — microbiological, chemical, pesticide residue — for each product category ensures imported goods meet Canadian safety limits and are defensible against CFIA sampling programs.

Canadian bilingual labeling requirements, nutrition facts tables, allergen declarations, and country-of-origin rules are complex and strictly enforced. Label review catches non-compliances before products hit retail shelves.

title: Regulatory & Audit Readiness
description: Systems, documentation, and training that keep you inspection-ready — every day, not just audit day.

slides.detail: Whether facing a CFIA routine inspection, BRCGS certification audit, or a major customer audit, on-site advisory provides real-time guidance on document presentation, corrective action responses, and auditor communication.

International regulatory divergences — between Codex Alimentarius, EU regulations, FDA requirements, and Canadian SFCR — are identified and interpreted to support market access strategies without duplicating compliance effort.

Accurate nutritional value calculations using validated databases and compliant formatting for Canadian Nutrition Facts tables and international equivalents ensures labels meet retail buyer and regulatory requirements at launch.
